what: Elanco makes medicines for animals: parasite treatments and vaccines for pets, and antibiotics, vaccines and feed additives for cattle, pigs and poultry. It was spun out of Eli Lilly.
customers: Veterinarians and pet owners, and livestock farmers buying through distributors.
money: flea and tick treatments, dermatology and pain medicines
vaccines, antibiotics and productivity products for livestock
moat: Approved animal drugs with patents and a veterinary sales force, in a market with far fewer entrants than human pharmaceuticals.
risks: Still posts a net loss of $147M, weighed down by amortisation from the Bayer animal health purchase
Revenue has been flat around $4.4B for several years
opportunities: $408M of free cash flow and analysts see about 19% upside
Three new pet dermatology and parasiticide products launched into the largest and most profitable category
Pet medicine spending holds up through downturns better than most consumer spending
watch: Pet Health revenue growth and the uptake of the new dermatology products.
